content.overview: Article 66 provides that the Vice-President shall be elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, and the voting at such election shall be by secret ballot. Qualifications mirror those for President in material respects (citizen, 35 years, qualified for Rajya Sabha membership), with an office-of-profit bar.
content.glance: VP elected by both Houses of Parliament (STV, secret ballot). Citizen; age ≥35; qualified for RS; no office of profit.
content.study:
Article 66:
- Electoral college: members of both Houses of Parliament (unlike President, State MLAs are not included).
- Method: proportional representation by single transferable vote; secret ballot.
- Qualifications: citizen of India; completed 35 years; qualified for election as a member of the Council of States; must not hold office of profit (with exclusions similar in spirit to Art 58).

Examination: contrast with Presidential electoral college (Art 54 includes State MLAs); STV; RS qualification (not LS).

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Electoral college: members of both Houses of Parliament.
2. STV; secret ballot.
3. Qualifications: citizen; ≥35 years; qualified for RS membership; no office of profit.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How is the Vice-President elected?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 66, the Vice-President is elected by the members of both Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, and the voting is by secret ballot. A candidate must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years of age, qualified for election as a member of the Council of States, and must not hold an office of profit.

examTips: Both Houses only (no State MLAs); STV; RS qualification; age 35.

keyTakeaways: Art 66: VP elected by both Houses; STV; secret ballot.
